title: Hafelekar & Top of Innsbruck
name: Hafelekar & Top of Innsbruck
kurzbeschreibung: The Hafelekar at 2,334 m above sea level – Top of Innsbruck: from the historic old town to the summit of the Nordkette in just 30 minutes with 360° views of Karwendel and Inntal.
beschreibung:
Overview

The distinctive Hafelekarspitze forms the spectacular rooftop of the Nordkette at 2,334 metres above sea level and is revered as the Top of Innsbruck. In a pairing unique worldwide, the Nordkettenbahn links the urban city centre of Tyrol's capital Innsbruck directly with rugged high-alpine rock terrain in barely 30 minutes of travel time. From the futuristic Hungerburgbahn station in the city centre via the Seegrube up to the Hafelekar mountain station at 2,269 metres, visitors conquer more than 1,700 metres of elevation and savour an incomparable panoramic view over the Tyrolean Inntal and into the wild, untouched Karwendelgebirge.

Route & Requirements

The historic Nordkettenbahn originally opened in 1928; its valley and interchange stations were redesigned by world-renowned star architect Zaha Hadid featuring avant-garde fluid forms in white glass. From the Hafelekar mountain station, a paved, secured panoramic trail leads in just 10 to 15 minutes of walking up to the summit cross of the Hafelekarspitze at 2,334 m. From the summit, an astounding vertical vista unfolds: to the south, gaze straight down onto the rooftops and streets of Innsbruck, the Sill gorge, and the glaciated peaks of the Stubaier Alpen; to the north, the utterly wild, remote rocky kingdom of the Alpenpark Karwendel stretches as far as the eye can see. For climbers, the Hafelekar serves as the starting point for the famous Innsbrucker Klettersteig traversing seven steep Nordkette summits. In winter, intrepid freeriders plunge down the notorious Hafelekar-Rinne – with a gradient of up to 70%, one of the steepest ski routes in all of Europe.

Visit & Arrival

The Nordkettenbahn (comprising Hungerburgbahn, Seegrubenbahn, and Hafelekarbahn) operates year-round daily from 08:30 to 17:00 (with Friday and Saturday evening ascents to the Seegrube in summer). Top of Innsbruck return ticket prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €47.00, seniors approx. €42.00, youths approx. €37.50, children (aged 6 to 15) approx. €23.50. Holders of the Innsbruck Card enjoy free travel across all three sections! Car-free arrival: board the underground Hungerburgbahn directly in the heart of Innsbruck's historic old town at the station Congress / Hofburg. Alternatively by car to the car park at the Hungerburg or to the Seegrube valley station (city parking garages offer discounted rates with cable car ticket purchase).

Tips

The short summit trail from the mountain station to the Hafelekar cross is well developed and lined with safety railings, but surefootedness and sturdy walking shoes are still required. Stop off at the restaurant Seegrube by DoN and savour authentic Tyrolean culinary treats on the expansive panoramic sun terrace high above the city roofs.
